props.gloss_en: RSBG: [a dying animal's slaughter is valid only] once it convulses with hand and foot
R' Eliezer: it suffices if [its blood] spurted
R' Shimon: one who slaughtered at night and next morning found the walls full of blood -- valid, for it spurted, as R' Eliezer's measure
the Sages: once it convulses with hand or foot, or wags its tail
the mishna: a small animal that extended its foreleg and did not draw it back -- invalid, for that is only the soul's departure
[a slaughtered] animal in danger of dying is permitted -- the presupposition the Gemara seeks a source for
(entertained) 'these are the living ones you may eat': eat what lives, not what does not -- and a dying animal is not living, so it would be forbidden
the verse: you shall not eat a carcass (Deut 14:21)
the verse: you shall not eat a tereifa (Ex 22:30)
'the fat of a carcass and the fat of a tereifa' (Lev 7:24) -- and the Master said: let the carcass prohibition, and the tereifa prohibition, take effect upon the prohibition of forbidden fat
(entertained) the tereifa is the same as the dying animal
since the Merciful One wrote 'carcass', it follows that the tereifa is not the dying animal
why 'fat ... fat' twice? there is one whose fat is not distinguished from its meat, and another whose fat is distinguished from its meat -- and which is that? the dying animal
the verse (Ez 4:14): my soul has not been defiled, carcass and tereifa I have not eaten from my youth until now, nor has piggul meat come into my mouth
the baraita: 'my soul has not been defiled' -- I did not have thoughts by day that bring impurity by night
the baraita: 'carcass and tereifa I have not eaten' -- I never ate the meat of a 'slaughter-quick, slaughter-quick' animal
the baraita: 'nor has piggul meat come into my mouth' -- I did not eat of an animal about which a sage gave a ruling
in R' Natan's name they said: [piggul means] I did not eat of an animal whose priestly gifts were not separated
Rav: [a dying animal is] any that is stood up and does not stand
Rav: even if it eats fodder [it is a dying animal, if it cannot stand]
Rami bar Yechezkel: even if it eats beams
Rav (per his students, answering Shmuel's 'what did Rav say about the dying animal?'): if it lowed, excreted, or twitched its ear -- that is convulsion
Shmuel: did Abba need to strain his ears? I say: whatever [movement] is not one of the things a dead animal does [is convulsion]
Shmuel (as Rav Anan reports): if its leg was bent and it extended it -- that is a thing a dead animal does
Shmuel (as Rav Anan reports): extended and it bent it -- things a dead animal does not do
[from the mishna:] but if it drew [the leg] back -- valid
the baraita: R' Yosei said, R' Meir used to say: lowing at the time of slaughter is not convulsion
R' Elazar b. R' Yosei in his name: even if it excreted and wagged its tail, that is not convulsion
Rav Chisda: the convulsion they spoke of is at the end of the slaughter
what is 'at the end of the slaughter'? in the middle of the slaughter -- to exclude the start of the slaughter
the convulsion must come in the middle of the slaughter (not at its start)
the convulsion must come at the very end of the slaughter
Rava: any that does not do so at the end of the slaughter -- it is known that its soul was taken from it before
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the convulsion they spoke of is at the start of the slaughter
Shmuel: [the mishna's 'walls'] -- we learned the walls of the slaughter-cut
[R' Eliezer's] spurting is lighter than R' Gamliel's [measure] and superior to the Rabbis'
Avuha deBar Avuvram: the Rabbis are responding to R' Eliezer (were it R' Gamliel they would have said 'once it convulsed'); and if [spurting] were superior, what is 'until'?
the baraita (Lev 22:27): 'ox or sheep' excludes a hybrid, 'or goat' a look-alike, 'when born' one born by caesarean, 'seven days' one lacking time, 'under its mother' an orphan
the orphan is one where this one departed to death as that one departed to life
Rava: the halakha follows this baraita
the baraita: a small animal that extended its foreleg and did not draw it back -- invalid
the baraita: that is the foreleg; with the hind leg, whether extended and not bent or bent and not extended -- valid
the baraita: that is a small animal; a large one, foreleg or hind leg, either way -- valid
the baraita: and a bird -- even if it only fluttered its wing or only wagged its tail, that is convulsion

supports.gloss_en: מדאמר רחמנא נבלה לא תאכל -- if a dying animal were forbidden while alive, need it be said after death?

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא היינו נבלה היינו מסוכנת? -- perhaps 'carcass' is itself the dying animal

refuted_by.gloss_en: לא ס"ד, דכתיב וכי ימות (Lev 11:39): only after death does the Merciful One call it a carcass

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא לעולם: carcass and dying animal are one status -- alive it is forbidden by a positive command, after death by a prohibition (unanswered; the text turns with אלא)

supports.gloss_en: מדאמר רחמנא טרפה לא תאכל -- if the dying animal, which lacks nothing, were forbidden, need the tereifa be?

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא היינו טרפה היינו מסוכנת, to violate a positive command and a prohibition

refuted_by.gloss_en: אם כן נבלה למה לי? if alive it is under a prohibition and a positive command, need it be said after death?

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא carcass = tereifa = dying animal, to violate two prohibitions and a positive command (unanswered; the text turns with אלא)

supports.gloss_en: were tereifa the dying animal, the verse should say 'the fat of a tereifa you shall not eat' and the carcass would follow a fortiori; since 'carcass' is written, tereifa is not the dying animal

deflected_by.gloss_en: מתקיף לה מר בר רב אשי: perhaps tereifa is the dying animal, and 'carcass' is written for a carcass not arising from a dying animal -- one made a gistera

refuted_by.gloss_en: התם נמי: there too it cannot but be a dying animal briefly before most [of the neck] is severed

supports.gloss_en: ואיבעית אימא: if so, let it say 'the fat of a carcass and a tereifa' -- why 'fat ... fat'? there is one whose fat is distinguished from its meat: the dying animal
if it is permitted, that is Ezekiel's distinction [in never eating 'slaughter-quick' meat]; if it were forbidden, what would be Ezekiel's distinction?
מנא אמינא לה? the mishna: extended its foreleg and did not draw it back -- invalid. When? if at the end of slaughter, would it go on living? rather, in the middle

deflected_by.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבא: לעולם at the end -- any that does not do so at the end, its soul evidently departed before

supports.gloss_en: מנא אמינא לה? R' Shimon's mishna -- walls full of blood, valid -- and Shmuel: the walls of the slaughter-cut. Fine if [the sign] is at the start; if at the end, perhaps it spurted at the start

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודלמא שאני זינוק, דעדיף -- perhaps spurting is different, being superior

refuted_by.gloss_en: ומי עדיף? והתנן: R' Eliezer says it suffices if it spurted -- lighter than R' Gamliel

supports.gloss_en: דתנן, אמר רבי שמעון: השוחט בלילה ולמחר מצא כתלים מלאים דם -- כשרה, שזינקה

מנא אמינא לה? דתניא: 'under its mother' excludes the orphan -- which can only be one whose mother died as it was born; that needs a verse only if vitality is required at the end of birth, otherwise 'when born' would teach it
האי יתום היכי דמי? -- not born and then orphaned (would the mother live forever?), nor orphaned before birth (that is 'when born'); so this one departed to death as that one to life
תנינא: בהמה דקה שפשטה ידה ולא החזירה -- פסולה; הא החזירה -- כשרה
